svg.aria-label: Basic terms for identifying plants (schematic): leaf arrangement is alternate, opposite, whorled or basal (rosette); leaves are simple or compound, and compound leaves are pinnate, palmate or trifoliate; leaf margins are entire, toothed or lobed; venation is net-veined (mostly dicots) or parallel (mostly monocots); a stem may be round or square in cross-section (square stems are common in the mint family), hollow or solid, and a stem that oozes white milky sap when broken needs extra care; inflorescences are umbels, compound umbels (carrot family), heads (daisy family: what looks like one flower is many florets), spikes, racemes and panicles. It is easy to misidentify a plant from one leaf or one piece of root: identify it when the plant is whole, ideally in flower or fruit, look at root, stem, leaves, flowers and fruit, and check at least 3 features
svg.title: Basic terms for identifying plants

g.text: Basic terms for identifying plants (for source-plant identification)
(Schematic: outlines only, to help you read floras and the descriptions in the later chapters)
① Leaf arrangement: how leaves sit on the stem
⑤ Stem: shape in cross-section? Hollow or solid? Milky sap?
⑥ Inflorescence: how flowers are arranged on the axis
⚠️ It is easy to misidentify a plant from one leaf or one piece of root
Identify it when the plant is whole, ideally in flower or fruit; look at root, stem, leaves, flowers and fruit,
and check at least 3 features for each herb
